title: SB Mart Daily Sales
masthead_sub: Wednesday 12 August 2026 · scored against past Wednesdays in week 2 of the month · ST1 and ST4 · all figures in USD

hero.headline: Net Sales landed USD 98.79 under the floor of its normal band, and USD 7.1K under the benchmark.
hero.narrative: Bills held up — 5,780 against a benchmark of 5,981, inside the normal band. What fell was the amount in each basket. All of the shortfall against the floor sits in ST4; ST1 finished level with its own floor.

stats.label: Net Sales · −USD 98.79 against its P20 floor

bridge.note: Starting from the benchmark of USD 76.4K: 201 fewer Bills took off USD 2.6K, and each basket holding USD 0.78 less took off USD 4.5K. The smaller basket is 64% of the gap. The two add to USD 7.1K exactly.

stores.headline: USD 38.0K · level with its P20 floor

look_down.sentence: Inside ST4, the department below its own band is CONSUMER GOODS: USD 14.2K, −USD 1.3K against its P20 floor. Both stores are shown because a group figure hides a store: ST1 finished level with its own floor at USD 38.0K; ST4 finished USD 98.79 below its own floor at USD 31.3K.

caveats.lead: This is a comparison with the normal band, never with last year.
caveats.body: Every figure is Wednesday 12 August 2026 placed against past days that match on the same weekday, so a Wednesday is only ever judged against other Wednesdays. The report holds no same-day-last-year figure and does not claim one.

caveats.lead: The figures cover ST1 and ST4 only
caveats.body: , and both stores are in every total on this page.

caveats.lead: The bands are built from a small number of matching days.
caveats.body: Net Sales, Bills and Basket Value use 25 matching past days; Margin uses 13 same-weekday readings. A band drawn from a short run of days is wider and moves more than one drawn from a long run.

caveats.lead: Net Sales arrives on two scales in the source, and has been put on one.
caveats.body: Net Sales for each store and for the whole business is published on one scale in the source, while every benchmark band, every cost and every Net Sales figure below store level is published on another exactly 3.7037 times larger. Two independent measurements taken from this run's own rows agree on that figure, so the second set has been brought onto the first. Every level then adds up to the whole business. Department, section and category Net Sales each add up to the whole-business figure exactly, which is the check that this was done right.

caveats.lead: A band at one level will not add up to the band at the level above it.
caveats.body: The whole day finished USD 98.79 below its floor while CONSUMER GOODS alone was USD 1.4K below its own. Each level is worked out separately, so the two do not match and neither is wrong.

One basket holding bread, shampoo and a shirt is one Bill for the store but appears under each department, section and category it touched. Each figure on this page is taken from its own level, and department shares of baskets do not add to 100%.

A name at department, section or category level can cover more than one group in the source, and the source does not carry the code that separates them. Net Sales for those names is added, which is safe. Their bands are added too, which is close but is not a true benchmark for the whole name, and their Bills count some baskets more than once. Treat a band at these levels as a guide.

caveats.lead: One department, OTHER, recorded no sale on this day
caveats.body: and has been left out of the tables rather than shown as a zero.
That is the most recent day the report holds. Last updated 12 Aug 2026.
